briefing.headline: You don't own Bruno Fernandes — 97.7% of the top 10k own him and 93.3% captain him — and with £0.1m in the bank the only routes to him are a wildcard or a two-transfer move, which is free next week if you bank this week's transfer.

do.action: Bank the free transfer this week (assuming you're not wildcarding).
do.why: With 1 FT you go to 2 in GW5, which pays for Haaland → Thiago and Cherki → B.Fernandes with no hit. Doing that pair now costs 4 points; waiting one week costs roughly 2.4 (Fernandes 6.11 vs Cherki 3.46 next GW, partly offset by Haaland 5.24 vs Thiago 4.95). Banking is the cheaper path to the same squad. The money works: out £15.5m + £7.8m, in £8.0m + £12.0m, leaving £3.4m headroom, so it survives even if your selling prices are below the listed ones.

do.action: Fix the bench order: van Ewijk first outfield sub, then Maguire, then Kusi-Asare.
do.why: Kusi-Asare is above van Ewijk in the order at 0.41 xP next and 2.3 over five, against van Ewijk's 3.64 and 16.6 and Maguire's 2.85 and 15.4. This is free points on any auto-sub week.

do.action: Move the vice-captaincy off Cherki to Mbeumo.
do.why: Cherki is on 3.46 xP next with 57 minutes a game and 88% play probability; Mbeumo is 5.26 with 86 minutes and 96%. If your captain blanks minutes you want the better armband behind him.

consider.action: Play the wildcard — but only after the final data refresh, not on this bundle.
consider.why: For: rank 5,601,933, £0.1m in the bank, a dead squad slot in Kusi-Asare (2.3 over five gameweeks, 49 career minutes), and you are off the top-10k core almost everywhere it matters — Fernandes 97.7%, Calafiori 78.0%, Calvert-Lewin 61.3%, Isak 57.3%, Raya 55.7%, all unowned. A wildcard buys Fernandes plus three or four of those in one move, which the two-transfer plan cannot. Against: your XI is not broken (nine of eleven starters at 3.4 xP or better next week), the first chip set runs to GW19 so there is no urgency, and this data was generated on 5 September for a 12 September deadline — a week of international-break news is missing. If you wildcard, do it on Friday's numbers, and build the squad around Fernandes.

consider.action: Take the -4 now for Fernandes instead of waiting (Haaland → Thiago, Cherki → Fernandes).
consider.why: For: it gains 7.7 over five gameweeks before the hit (Fernandes 33.0 for Cherki 19.5, Thiago 24.2 for Haaland 30.0), net +3.7, and it gets you the player 93.3% of the top 10k captain a week earlier. Against: 3.7 over five weeks is inside the model's error bars, and waiting one week gets the same squad for nothing. Only worth it if you fear a Fernandes price rise or you expect to wildcard later anyway.

consider.action: Whether to keep Haaland at all.
consider.why: He is 71.2% owned overall but only 10.0% among the top 10k — so holding him is a differential against the managers you want to catch, and a shield against the millions you are currently ranked among. His 30.0 over five is the second-best number in the whole dataset, but £15.5m of a £100.1m squad is why you cannot reach a £12.0m midfielder. Selling him is the enabling move, not a downgrade you make for its own sake.

ignore.action: Using the free transfer to replace Kusi-Asare.
ignore.why: There is no forward at or below £4.6m worth owning in the top-60 list — the cheapest are Awoniyi and Barry at £5.5m. He is a bench slot; the fix is a wildcard, not a transfer you cannot fund.

ignore.action: Bench Boost or Free Hit this week.
ignore.why: No blanks or doubles in GW4, and your four bench players total 9.02 xP next gameweek (Kinsky 2.12, Maguire 2.85, Kusi-Asare 0.41, van Ewijk 3.64). Neither chip has a trigger.

ignore.action: Swapping Cherki out of the XI for van Ewijk to go 4-4-2.
ignore.why: It is worth 0.18 xP (3.64 against 3.46) and van Ewijk's number rests on 180 minutes this season. Not worth reshaping the side for, and it disappears anyway once Cherki is sold.

ignore.action: The cheap model darlings — Tavernier (23.3 over five, 2.3% owned), Scott, Wharton, Canvot.
ignore.why: They score well because FPL's FDR is blunt and the model rewards bulk minutes at low prices. You are 5.6m in the rank table because you lack the core, not because you lack differentials.

captain.why: João Pedro leads your squad at 5.98 xP next with Hull at home (FDR 2), ahead of Mbeumo 5.26, Szoboszlai 5.24 and Haaland 5.24 away at United (FDR 4). The uncomfortable part: 93.3% of the top 10k captain B.Fernandes and you cannot, so you are taking an unwanted differential armband whatever you do this week — 97.0% of them own João Pedro but only 1.3% captain him. That is the clearest statement of why the Fernandes move matters more than any single week's captain choice.

briefing.chips: No chip should be played in GW4 on these numbers: no double, no blank, and a bench worth 9.02 points. Triple Captain is already gone from set one (used in GW3), leaving wildcard, Free Hit and Bench Boost to be used by the GW19 deadline — plenty of time. The wildcard is the only live question, and it is a decision to make on Friday's refreshed data, not this bundle.
risks: The data is seven days old (generated 5 September for a 12 September deadline) and covers an international break — injuries, suspensions and Rotowire lineups will all move before you confirm anything.

Fernandes at £12.0m may rise before GW5; if he does, the two-transfer route still clears with £3.4m of headroom, but check your actual selling prices in the app, as the model assumes you sell at current price.
Thiago's run after GW4 is hard — CHE(H)4, AVL(A)4, LIV(H)4 — so the 24.2 over five is front-loaded and he could look a poor swap for Haaland by GW6.
Selling Haaland at 71.2% overall ownership is a real risk against the field you are actually ranked in; a hat-trick week undoes several gameweeks of this plan.
Cherki's 3.46 assumes 57 minutes and 88% play; if he nails down a starting role at City the case for selling him weakens.
The GW5 plan assumes you make no transfer in GW4 and take no hit — any deviation drops you back to one free transfer and the Fernandes move costs 4.
